_comment: Which captured image backs which finding, and what the reviewer is looking at. A finding with no image says so rather than borrowing one.

F-01.caption: The script requested /pm and landed on /pm/event/atp-faria-alcaraz-2026-09-02. The stored tab in localStorage reopened the previous market and rewrote the address bar.

F-02.caption: The two price sets as they were read from document.body.innerText on 3 September, side by side with the sum of each. This is a rendering of the captured text, not of the screen; the raw capture is published beside it. Stated on the image: it did not reproduce on the newer build, which is why the frequency is answered It only happened once.

F-03.caption: Settlement Time reads Sep 9, 3:00 PM UTC on a market that shows a final score of 2-6, is marked Resolved, and has its order book closed. The match was played on 2 September.

F-04.caption: The card text as captured, showing Extra Innings with no price and both order buttons still active, and the same card on a later reload where the price was present. A rendering of the captured text; the raw capture is published beside it.

F-05.caption: The default Trending grid, which is where resolved markets are promoted with live buy buttons.

F-06.caption: The percentage values extracted from the page in a single render, with the one decimal value marked. The re-test result is stated on the image: 99.5% was the only decimal on the newer build, which narrows the claim to the 100.0% case.

F-07.caption: Every prop label repeats the full event title before the part that identifies it, so the rail truncates exactly where the distinguishing text begins. 48 rows carry the prefix.

F-08.caption: The same rail, showing 13 rows rendering "-- Vol" beside neighbours that show $4K Vol and $116 Vol.

F-09.caption: The preload warnings Chrome emitted during one load of the trading route, with the chunk and resource counts measured in the same load. Chrome reports this waste itself; the full console capture is published beside the image.

F-11.caption: Both 2028 cards render in this grid at the same time, one spelling the candidate "J.D. Vance" and the other "JD Vance".

F-12.caption: Before: a search for bitcoin has narrowed the grid to matching markets, and the query is in the box.
After one click on the Politics chip: the search box is empty and the query is gone. Read back from the DOM immediately afterwards, both search inputs returned an empty string.

F-13.caption: The subcategory rail, where entries showing a count of 0 are still offered as selectable filters.

F-14.caption: At 375x812 the subcategory rail scrolls horizontally, so the filter responsible for an empty result can sit off-screen with no control to clear it.

F-15.caption: The directory whose inactive responsive layout stays focusable at zero size, putting invisible stops in the keyboard tab order ahead of the first market card.

F-16.caption: The nav reads "August Rewards", captured with the browser clock in the same run at 2026-09-03T09:46:37Z.

F-18.caption: app.manic.trade/pm rendering inside an iframe on a page served from an unrelated origin. The market grid, live prices and the Log In button are all present, and the browser raised no framing objection.

F-19.caption: The full response headers for /pm. CSP, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy are all absent; the is-mobile cookie carries neither Secure nor HttpOnly.

F-20.caption: Three invented market slugs, each served as HTTP 200 with 1.5 MB and the generic landing-page title, against control routes that 404 correctly.

F-22.caption: Heading and landmark counts taken from the HTML the server returns: zero h1, h2 and h3 on both the directory and an event page, and two <main> elements on each.

F-23.caption: The Open Graph and meta description served for a market that resolved on 2 September, still reading "Ends Sep 9".

F-24.caption: Two missing paths, each answered with 1,512,170 bytes of application HTML.

F-25.caption: A Slackbot-agent request stopped at each byte cap. Below 512 KB the page yields no title and no description at all; the byte offsets underneath show why.

F-26.caption: The Open Graph description served for itf-danil-laro-2026-09-04, reading Completed Match, 50%, and Ends Sep 11 in one string.

F-27.caption: The network the /pm directory makes on its own with no interaction: 58 calls, 17.4 MB, 8,610 event objects returned, 24 cards drawn.

F-28.caption: Heading counts per route, read from the hydrated DOM. The referral page carries two top-level headings where the root carries one and /pm carries none.

F-29.caption: The Ends date compared against the date in each slug across 45 dated markets. Twenty-eight are correct; fifteen sit at exactly seven days, with nothing in between.

F-30.caption: The string August present in the rendered text of three routes, with the browser clock reading 4 September in the same run.

F-31.caption: Controls exposing no text, aria-label, title or labelled image. Four on the landing page; none on the leaderboard or referral pages.

F-32.caption: 194 markets carry a score while still flagged acceptingOrders; the box shows one verified live - a finished match (period FT, Pegula won 1-6 6-4 6-3) still status live and accepting orders at an ask of 1.0. A rendering of the exact API bytes; the raw capture is published beside it.

F-33.caption: 338 of 6,519 events had an end timestamp already in the past while still accepting orders and not closed. Rendered from the scan output; raw capture beside it.

F-34.caption: 81 events whose advertised end time falls before their start time, each 12 hours out. From the events API; raw capture beside it.

F-35.caption: 47 outcomes marked active=false while still acceptingOrders=true. From the events API; raw capture beside it.

F-36.caption: 30 outcomes and 25 events reporting a 24-hour volume larger than their all-time volume. From the events API; raw capture beside it.

F-37.caption: Both security.txt locations return 404 while robots.txt and sitemap.xml are present, so the well-known mechanism works and only the security contact is missing. curl headers; raw capture beside it.

F-38.caption: /manifest.json and /favicon.ico each answered with HTTP 404 carrying 1,512,158 bytes of HTML under content-type text/html. curl headers; raw capture beside it.

F-39.caption: The 5-minute BTC and ETH up/down markets, where the displayed chance sits 22 points away from the mid of the live order book. From the events API; raw capture beside it.

F-40.caption: One image host across all 6,521 events: polymarket-upload.s3.amazonaws.com. From the events API; raw capture beside it.

F-41.caption: Nine events rendering two outcomes with the identical name. From the events API; raw capture beside it.

F-42.caption: Read-only from the events API: all 12 finished (FT) markets in the snapshot were still accepting orders, with 8 impossible outcomes still carrying an executable ask. The worked example is a 7-0 final where Draw, 0-0, and the loser scoring first are each still buyable. No order was placed; the confirming step is left to a funded account.
